abilitySource: a debt owed by an ancestor
a song learned in a dream
a craft passed mother to daughter
a name given at a naming ceremony
the last speaker of a language
abilityEffect: lets the dead finish one sentence
lets a crowd share one memory
shifts luck from one person to another
borrows the skills of an ancestor for a day
tells the true name of a place
turns grief into a physical shield
lets roads lead only where you are welcome
makes stone soft for a heartbeat
slows time for whoever is listening
abilityCost: must be repaid with a story
only works for others, never yourself
erases your reflection a little more
makes you forget a word of your mother tongue
must be shared equally or it sours
costs the trust of an animal ally
characterWant: to win back the family land
to learn the song nobody sings anymore
to be free of an inherited debt
characterWound: lost their language in a foreign school
carries a name that belonged to someone else
was exiled for telling the truth
survived a fire that took the archive
was chosen over a more worthy sibling
characterContradiction: a seer who refuses to look
an elder who acts like a child
a guardian who longs to wander
storySpark: A market opens that only trades in memories.
The river refuses to flow until a promise is kept.
Every child born this season speaks an extinct language.
A masquerade appears with no one inside.
Two rival families must share one sacred drum.
The city's founding story is proven false.
A storyteller's tales start coming true.
A comet returns, and with it a forgotten ruler.
The wedding guests arrive from a century ago.
placeKind: a market on the back of a sleeping beast
a caravanserai at the edge of the salt flats
a city in a baobab grove
a village that moves with the herds
placeFeature: where the dead are welcome one night a year
whose streets rearrange at every festival
that only appears at low tide
guarded by a lineage of smiths
whose walls are written with ancestors' names
where every bridge is a promise
that sings when the wind comes from the sea
where time runs slower near the well
placeSecret: it was founded on a broken treaty
the river spirit still owns the land
it is the shell of an older city
its queen is a story that came true
a gate to the sky world lies beneath the market
placeEra: in the age of the founding ancestors
in a future the elders foretold
conflictCause: a prophecy each side reads differently
a new tax on the salt road
a sacred grove cut for timber
conflictStakes: who may speak for the ancestors
the right to name the city
a hostage child raised by the enemy
the loyalty of the sea spirits
conflictTwist: both sides worship the same spirit
it began with a translator's error
a third power profits from every battle
the losing side writes the history
the truce is kept only by children
one side's hero is the other's monster

twists: Root the power in community: who else must take part for it to work?
Add a cultural cost — a taboo, an obligation, a debt to ancestors.
Invert it: what if the power only works on its user, or only for others?
Change the medium: make it sung, woven, cooked, drummed or written.
Tie it to place: a river, a mountain, a crossroads, a city.
Make it inherited across generations, changing each time it passes down.
Give it a sensory signature no one else uses (a smell, a rhythm, a taste).
Limit it by time: a season, a festival, a moon phase.
Make the side-effect more interesting than the effect.
Ask: whose story is this? Who in the culture would tell it differently?

mapStyles.name: Ink & Mist
mapStyles.inspiration: East Asian shan shui (mountain-water) ink painting and scroll maps
mapStyles.care: Inspired by, not imitating, specific painters or sacred scrolls.

mapStyles.name: Idrisi Atlas (south-up)
mapStyles.inspiration: al-Idrisi's Tabula Rogeriana (1154) and other Islamic-world maps that place south at the top

mapStyles.name: Codex Path (east-up)
mapStyles.inspiration: Mesoamerican codex and lienzo maps (e.g. Codex Mendoza, Mapa de Cuauhtinchan) with footprint roads and place glyphs
mapStyles.care: Use the visual grammar (footprints, glyphs) without copying sacred or historical glyphs.

mapStyles.name: Swell & Stick Chart
mapStyles.inspiration: Marshall Islands navigation charts (mattang, meddo, rebbelib) that map ocean swells
mapStyles.care: Real stick charts were personal memory aids of trained navigators; this is an homage, not a usable chart.

mapStyles.name: Mandala Cosmos
mapStyles.inspiration: Hindu, Buddhist and Jain cosmological maps with Mount Meru at the centre
mapStyles.care: Mandalas can be sacred objects; design your own cosmology rather than reproducing a ritual mandala.

mapStyles.name: Star Road
mapStyles.inspiration: Night-sky wayfinding: Polynesian star compasses and Andean dark-cloud constellations

mapStyles.name: Mud Cloth
mapStyles.care: Bogolanfini motifs carry meanings; use the palette and rhythm, credit the tradition.

traitTemplates.name: Ember eyes
traitTemplates.description: Eyes that glow faintly in darkness.

traitTemplates.name: Spirit-sight
traitTemplates.description: Sees spirits. Often skips generations; not every carrier awakens.

traitTemplates.name: Feather & scale pattern
traitTemplates.description: Two marks that blend when inherited together.

traitTemplates.name: Stormblood
traitTemplates.description: Carried on the X chromosome — often seen in XY children of XX carriers.

traitTemplates.name: Height
traitTemplates.description: Many genes plus nutrition; children cluster around the parents' average.

traitTemplates.name: River-gift (one line)
traitTemplates.description: Passes only through one chosen parent's line (e.g. the mother's), like a matrilineal inheritance.

traitTemplates.name: Chosen by the ancestors
traitTemplates.description: The ancestors choose; family helps but doesn't decide.

speciesTemplates.name: Humans
speciesTemplates.roots: Everyone — vary appearance, culture and language as widely as the real world does.
speciesTemplates.care: Avoid treating one human culture as the default.

speciesTemplates.name: Fox-spirits
speciesTemplates.roots: Huli jing (China), kitsune (Japan), gumiho (Korea).
speciesTemplates.appearance: Foxes who gain tails and power with age; can take human form.
speciesTemplates.care: Each tradition differs — kitsune can be benevolent messengers of Inari; gumiho are often dangerous.

speciesTemplates.name: Nāga
speciesTemplates.roots: Serpent beings of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain traditions; Mekong nāga.
speciesTemplates.appearance: Great serpents or half-serpent people guarding waters and treasures.
speciesTemplates.care: Revered in living religions — avoid making them generic monsters.

speciesTemplates.name: Jinn
speciesTemplates.roots: Beings of smokeless fire with free will, from pre-Islamic and Islamic belief.
speciesTemplates.care: Part of Islamic belief; resist the ‘genie in a lamp’ cliché and Orientalism.

speciesTemplates.name: Aziza
speciesTemplates.roots: Forest beings of Fon (Dahomey) tradition who teach hunters magic and herbal knowledge.
speciesTemplates.care: Draw on Fon sources; credit the tradition.

speciesTemplates.name: Mmoatia
speciesTemplates.roots: Little forest people of Akan folklore, skilled in herbs.

speciesTemplates.name: Trickster animal people
speciesTemplates.roots: Anansi the spider (Akan), Kalulu the hare (Central & East Africa), Br'er Rabbit (African American).

speciesTemplates.name: Tengu
speciesTemplates.roots: Mountain bird-folk of Japanese folklore, masters of martial arts.

speciesTemplates.name: Dokkaebi
speciesTemplates.roots: Korean goblins with magic clubs who love wrestling and pranks.

speciesTemplates.name: Encantados
speciesTemplates.roots: Amazonian river-dolphin people who come ashore for festivals.

speciesTemplates.name: Duende
speciesTemplates.roots: Household and forest spirits of Iberian, Latin American and Filipino folklore.

speciesTemplates.name: Water people
speciesTemplates.roots: Selkies (Scotland), ningyo (Japan), iara (Brazil); Mami Wata (West & Central Africa).
speciesTemplates.care: Mami Wata is a living spiritual tradition — treat with respect.

speciesTemplates.name: Migoi / Yeti
speciesTemplates.roots: Wild mountain beings of Himalayan folklore.

speciesTemplates.name: Garuda-kin
speciesTemplates.roots: The divine bird Garuda and the bird-people of Hindu and Buddhist myth.
speciesTemplates.care: Garuda is sacred; build your own bird-folk inspired by, not copying, him.

speciesTemplates.name: Golems
speciesTemplates.roots: Clay figures animated by sacred words in Jewish folklore (e.g. the Golem of Prague).

speciesTemplates.name: Aswang
speciesTemplates.roots: Shapeshifting ghouls of Filipino folklore.
speciesTemplates.care: The label has been used to stigmatise real people, especially women; handle with care.

speciesTemplates.name: Boo hags & plat-eyes
speciesTemplates.roots: Gullah Geechee folklore: boo hags ride sleepers at night; plat-eyes are shapeshifting spirits of the marsh.
speciesTemplates.care: From living Gullah culture — credit it.

speciesTemplates.name: Duppies & jumbies
speciesTemplates.roots: Spirits of the dead in Jamaican (duppy) and Eastern Caribbean (jumbie) folklore.

speciesTemplates.name: Soucouyant & Ol' Higue
speciesTemplates.roots: Skin-shedding fireball women of Trinidad (soucouyant) and Guyana (Ol' Higue).
speciesTemplates.care: Like other ‘witch’ figures, the label has been used against real women.

speciesTemplates.name: Rougarou / lougarou
speciesTemplates.roots: Shapeshifters of Louisiana Creole and Haitian folklore.
